detailed_findings.finding: The argument K_{m,g} \subseteq S_{m,g} is correct: the extra defining inequalities of K_{m,g} only restrict the set of positive tuples summing to g.
The finiteness proof for S_{m,g} is complete: each coordinate satisfies 1 <= a_r <= g when g>=1, so S_{m,g} is contained in a finite Cartesian product.
The edge case g=0 is correctly handled: no positive integer tuple can have sum 0, so S_{m,g} is empty.

reason: The proof correctly shows finiteness by bounding K_{m,g} inside the set of positive integer (m-1)-tuples summing to g, and then bounding that set inside the finite box {1,...,g}^{m-1} for g>=1, with the g=0 case handled separately by emptiness. This fully establishes the lemma and matches the intended semantic role.
